facts.statement: A fossil site known as a Konservat-Lagerstätte was discovered in 2006 in the Hami region of Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: In 2006, a Konservat-Lagerstätte was reported from the Shengjinkou Formation in the Hami region of Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The holotype of Hamititan consists of seven preserved tail vertebrae with three chevrons.
facts.quote: Among the excavated fossils were seven caudal vertebrae with three chevrons preserved. These were established as the holotype (HM V22) of the new sauropod taxon, Hamititan.

facts.statement: A theropod tooth found near the holotype suggests the dinosaur was preyed upon shortly after death.
facts.quote: A theropod tooth was found near the sixth caudal vertebra of the holotype. It is likely that this theropod preyed on the holotype shortly after it died.

facts.statement: The species name xinjiangensis refers to the Chinese province of Xinjiang.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the city of Hami, where the holotype was found, while the specific name, xinjiangensis, refers to the Chinese province, Xinjiang.

facts.statement: Hamititan lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago in the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Hamititan xinjiangensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Hamititan de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace 120 millones de año durante el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Hamititan is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Hamititan (meaning "Hami giant") is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Shengjinkou Formation of Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: Hamititan is classified within the unranked family Titanosauria.
Phylogenetic analysis places Hamititan as a derived non-lithostrotian titanosaur related to Epachthosaurus, Kaijutitan, and Notocolossus.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis of Wang et al. places Hamititan as a derived non-lithostrotian titanosaur in a polytomy with Epachthosaurus, Kaijutitan, Notocolossus, rinconsaurs, lognkosaurs, and lithostrotians.

facts.statement: The time range for Hamititan is estimated between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Contemporary fauna at the Hamititan locality included the pterosaur Hamipterus and the sauropod Silutitan.
facts.quote: Other animals from the holotype locality include the pterosaur Hamipterus and contemporary euhelopodid Silutitan, which is described in the same paper.
